title: For female borrowers, increased pitch length may correlate with faster funding, contradicting the general trend.
Male borrowers who make explicit promises of timely repayment may fund more slowly.
Mentioning the specific number of children may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about education or social volunteering may fund more slowly.
While operational specificity generally accelerates funding, female borrowers who provide detailed lists of supplies or product types fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who use explicit gratitude markers in their pitches may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the educational needs of their children may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific loan amounts or the lending organization may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who address lenders directly in their pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention specific towns or regions in their pitch may fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention securing the future of their family fund faster.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about their children fund faster.
